messages:
maria: Quick update — ran an initial candidate scan across three new model variants for the chat product. Wanted to share a concise cost vs quality snapshot and get routing recommendations before we brief GTN.
alex: nice. which models? short bullets pls.
maria: models: calypso-8B-fp16 (baseline), calypso-8B-int8 (quantized), and nebula-7B-int4-mix (aggressive quant + remapped kernels). Testing on the standard product prompt set (5k prompts), latency budget 120ms p50, 300ms p99.
ryan: metrics? unit econ numbers? p50/p99, tokens/s, cost per 1k tokens.
maria: baseline (fp16) — p50 95ms / p99 260ms, quality pass rate 92.5% (eval suite), est cost $10.2 per 1k tokens. calypso-int8 — p50 88ms / p99 240ms, quality 91.7% (-0.8 pp), est cost $7.1 per 1k tokens. nebula-7B-int4-mix — p50 70ms / p99 210ms, quality 89.0% (-3.5 pp), est cost $4.5 per 1k tokens.
alex: helpful. do those quality drops show up on critical buckets (safety/intent/slot accuracy)?
maria: yes — breakdown: calypso-int8 has minor drift in long-form summarization coherence (~-1.2 pp) but safety and slot accuracy stable. nebula-int4 shows regressions concentrated in code completion and numeric reasoning (slot accuracy -4.1 pp), and a slight uptick in hallucination on multi-step instructions.
sophie: did you run any small-shot prompting or instruction-tuning mismatch checks? int4 can amplify failure modes in long contexts.
maria: ran 0-shot + 3-shot for a subset. int4 failures mostly under 3-shot long-context examples (seq len > 1k). We suspect KV cache precision degradation. Also observed some tokenization edge cases for nebula's tokenizer causing off-by-one in logits.
priya: from GTN perspective we need guidance: recommended default, fallback chain, and whether to expose quantized options to self-serve teams. Thoughts?
ryan: my take: calypso-int8 is a strong candidate for broad routing — ~30% cost drop for ~<1 pp quality loss and meets latency SLO. nebula-int4 could be used as a low-cost tier for non-critical batch workloads or high-throughput embeddings where slight quality loss is acceptable.
alex: agree. propose routing policy: primary = calypso-int8, fallback to calypso-fp16 on quality regression triggers, and nebula-int4 as async/batch-only. Add canary for 7 days with A/B (5% traffic) and monitor the eval set as well as product telemetry (NPS/error-rates).
maria: +1. I'll prepare a short scorecard for GTN: include p50/p99, cost delta, eval delta overall + per-bucket, and recommended routing. Draft snippet below.
maria: ```
Scorecard: calypso-int8 vs fp16
- latency: p50 -7ms, p99 -20ms
- cost: -30% ($7.1 vs $10.2 /1k)
- quality: -0.8 pp overall
- buckets: summarization -1.2 pp, safety ~0, slots ~0
Recommendation: Canary 5% -> primary routing on success; auto-fallback to fp16 on regression >1pp on eval or +0.5% product error-rate.
``` 
priya: perfect. include a short playbook for rollback triggers and telemetry checks (token-level cost, user-facing error signals, and eval regression). GTN will want expected savings vs risk for 3, 6, 12 month horizons.
maria: will add that. question for eng-runtime: do we need any kernel changes pinned for nebula-int4 to reduce numeric drift? @alex can you advise?
alex: quick note: nebula-int4 currently uses remapped gemm kernels + heuristic dequant. I think we should enable higher-precision KV caching for long-context flows (config flag: kv_cache_precision = "fp16") and re-run the long-context subset. That might recover ~1.5 pp of regression at ~+5% cost.
maria: good call. I'll spin that test. timeline: can we have a 5% canary config and runtime flags by EOD tomorrow? deploy-bot: schedule canary? :robot_face:
deploy-bot: Canary job created: calypso-int8 -> 5% traffic, duration 7d, monitors: eval-suite, product-errors, cost-delta. Canary ID: cny-2063456789-1
ryan: thanks. once canary runs let's also add a quick A/B conversion test for high-value customers (opt-in) so GTN can quantify revenue impact.
maria: noted. I'll post the GTN slide (one-pager) after the canary infra is live. tagging the thread for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
